findings.passage: “Voter ID has been the law of the land for 10 years in our state. This requirement has already undergone legal challenges and found to be constitutional. Everyone wants assurance their vote is counted. Since voter ID has become law in WI, voter participation has increased,” shared Rep. Goeben.
findings.note: Statement issued in her name after the Assembly passed the voter ID constitutional amendment 54 to 45. She says voter ID has been law for 10 years, was upheld in court, and that participation has risen since it began.

findings.passage: “I think it’s important to have this provision in our State Constitution as a safeguard from activist courts. Too often productive, thoughtful policy has been hijacked by an overreaching judiciary. This amendment reserves the right of the legislature to modify future requirements, as needed. Today, we have taken another step in ensuring safe elections, while preserving accessibility,” concluded Rep. Goeben.
findings.note: Same release. She gives her reasons for writing voter ID into the state constitution and says the legislature keeps the right to change future requirements.
